data.narrative: Alekhya demonstrated superior observability expertise, structured log literacy, and security awareness throughout Module 02. She effortlessly reconstructed request timelines from JSON telemetry, diagnosed Bug #3 (log level hardcoded override masking request lifecycles), and solved Bug #4 (UTC vs local naive timestamp mismatch causing midnight 404s). During the BREAK step, she immediately recognized the forged admin login as a CRLF Log Injection attack, identifying the timestamp timeline paradox and nesting inside user-controlled URL input.

dimension_scores.observation: Balanced cost and signal in logging strategy, selecting minimal-by-default to control cloud storage overhead while maintaining dynamic elevation capabilities
dimension_scores.evidence: I choose this strategy because it reduces storage costs and unnecessary log noise in production. We can keep INFO and WARN logs enabled by default and temporarily enable DEBUG logs when investigating a specific issue.

dimension_scores.observation: Used structured log fields (request_id, status_code, latency_ms) to trace end-to-end request lifecycles, and applied side-by-side timestamp comparison to resolve the midnight 404 mystery
dimension_scores.evidence: Traced r-003 client 404 in 10ms and r-004 DB latency in 680ms; pinpointed naive datetime.now() comparing against UTC created_at.

dimension_scores.observation: Identified CRLF Log Injection / Log Forging instantly, analyzing how attackers inject newlines to fabricate authenticated audit records and spoof SIEM alarms
dimension_scores.evidence: Bob inserted a newline character (\n) into the URL. If the application logs this untrusted input without proper handling, the newline can make the injected JSON look like a separate log entry. Sanitize and escape newline characters before logging.

dimension_scores.observation: Articulated the universal distributed systems timestamp contract: store and compare strictly in UTC, converting to local time only at presentation boundaries
dimension_scores.evidence: Always store timestamps in UTC and use timezone-aware datetime objects when comparing dates and times. Convert UTC to local time only when displaying it to users.

dimension_scores.observation: Delivered razor-sharp technical explanations with concrete code solutions for timezone-aware UTC queries and proactive watchdog log design
dimension_scores.evidence: from datetime import datetime, timezone; now_utc = datetime.now(timezone.utc); db.query(Link).filter(Link.code == code).filter(Link.created_at <= now_utc).first()

strengths: Flawless log literacy: easily reconstructs request lifecycles and isolates latency bottlenecks using structured JSON telemetry.
Strong security instincts: treats logs as an untrusted input boundary vulnerable to CRLF forgery.
Rigorous timestamp hygiene across distributed database and application boundaries.
growth_areas: Preparing for concurrency race conditions and minimal test reproduction scripts in Module 03.
data.recommendation: Proceed to Module 03: Minimal Reproduction & Flaky Failures.
